claims.text: LDMs decouple the image formation process into two stages: a perceptual compression phase and a generative phase.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states in Sec. 3 that the approach introduces 'an explicit separation of the compressive from the generative learning phase' and describes these as two distinct training phases.

claims.text: LDMs apply diffusion processes within the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder.
claims.reason: The paper's core contribution (Abstract, Sec. 3) is applying diffusion models 'in the latent space of powerful pretrained autoencoders' rather than pixel space.

claims.text: A time-conditional UNet performs the denoising process within the latent space.
claims.reason: Sec. 3.2 states 'The neural backbone εθ(◦, t) of our model is realized as a time-conditional UNet [71]'.

claims.text: The conditioning mechanism uses cross-attention layers that integrate external inputs such as text embeddings, class labels, or bounding boxes.
claims.reason: Sec. 3.3 explicitly describes cross-attention layers in the UNet backbone enabling conditioning on 'text or bounding boxes' and class labels.

claims.text: The autoencoder is trained using an adversarial objective combined with a perceptual loss and a regularization term (either KL-divergence or vector quantization).
claims.reason: Sec. 3.1 states the autoencoder uses 'a perceptual loss and a patch-based adversarial objective' with two regularization variants: 'KL-reg.' and 'VQ-reg.'.

claims.text: MS-COCO and LAION are used for text-to-image synthesis.
claims.reason: Sec. 4.3.1 states the text-to-image model was trained on 'LAION-400M' and evaluated on 'the MS-COCO validation set' (Tab. 2).

claims.text: Places is used for image inpainting.
claims.reason: Sec. 4.5 and Tab. 15 explicitly state the inpainting model uses the Places dataset, following the protocol of LaMa [88].

claims.text: Performance is quantitatively assessed using Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS) to measure image quality and diversity.
claims.reason: FID and IS are used throughout the experiments (Tab. 1, 2, 3, 5, 10) as the primary quantitative metrics for image generation quality.

claims.text: For super-resolution, PSNR and SSIM are employed.
claims.reason: Tab. 5 reports PSNR and SSIM for the x4 upscaling super-resolution experiments on ImageNet-Val.

claims.text: A user study utilizing a 2-alternative force-choice paradigm was conducted to evaluate human preference for inpainting and super-resolution tasks.
claims.reason: Sec. E.3.6 describes the '2-alternative force-choice paradigm' used in the user study covering both super-resolution and inpainting tasks (Tab. 4).

claims.text: LDMs achieve state-of-the-art results in inpainting and class-conditional synthesis.
claims.reason: The Abstract explicitly claims 'new state-of-the-art scores for image inpainting and class-conditional image synthesis', confirmed by results in Tab. 3 and Tab. 7.

claims.text: ImageNet is used for class-conditional image synthesis and super-resolution.
claims.reason: Tab. 15 confirms ImageNet as the dataset for both 'Class-Label-to-Image' and 'Super Resolution' tasks; Sec. 4.1 and 4.4 detail these experiments.

claims.text: The LDM is trained to predict the noise added to the latent representations using a reweighted variational objective.
claims.reason: Sec. 3.2 presents the LDM objective (Eq. 2) as predicting added noise εθ(zt, t) in latent space using a reweighted variational bound.

claims.text: The authors employ classifier-free guidance to improve visual quality and fidelity during inference.
claims.reason: Sec. 4.3.1 states 'applying classifier-free diffusion guidance [32] greatly boosts sample quality', and it is used for both text-to-image (Tab. 2) and class-conditional (Tab. 3) models.

claims.text: CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, and LSUN are used for unconditional image generation.
claims.reason: Sec. 4.2 explicitly trains 'unconditional models of 256^2 images on CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, LSUN-Churches and -Bedrooms' and reports results in Tab. 1.
